claims: NASA's Artemis II is scheduled for launch on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon.
Artemis II serves as a critical test flight for future lunar landings.
SpaceX is not directly responsible for the Artemis II launch.
SpaceX is developing the Starship HLS (Human Landing System) for landing astronauts on the lunar surface during later missions.
Artemis II mission will use NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) Orion capsule.
SpaceX has a contract to provide the Human Landing System (HLS) for future later-phase Artemis lunar landings.
SpaceX's Starship is expected to be used to land humans on the Moon as early as Artemis III or subsequent missions.
The Artemis II SLS rocket launch is expected to be visible in parts of Florida and Georgia.
Artemis II SLS rocket launch from Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center.
SpaceX is not launching the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis program is designed to return humans to the Moon.
